title: Minjin Kim
text:
Research Areas







Corpus Linguistics


I use corpus-based and computational approaches to examine language use across English and Korean, with interests in learner language, academic discourse, and disciplinary communication. I am also interested in developing corpus-informed resources for language teaching and research and in extending these approaches to less commonly taught languages.









Second Language Acquisition


I investigate how second language learners develop and use language across proficiency levels, time, tasks, and modalities, with attention to developmental patterns, variability, and individual learner trajectories.









AI-Mediated Language Learning & Assessment


I investigate how generative AI, speech technologies, and other computational tools can mediate language learning, feedback, interaction, and assessment.









Critical & Research-Informed AI Use


I explore how AI can be used critically and responsibly in language education, with an emphasis on SLA theory, evidence-based practice, and the evaluation and verification of AI-generated feedback.

title: Minjin Kim
text:
Minjin Kim


I am an Assistant Professor of Second Language Studies, TESOL, and Korean in the Department of Linguistics, Languages, and Cultures at Michigan State University. I serve as Director of the Korean Program and Co-Director of the Second Language Studies Corpus Lab. I earned my Ph.D. in Applied Linguistics from Pennsylvania State University.
My research focuses on corpus linguistics, second language acquisition, and language learning and technology, with a particular interest in generative AI. More broadly, I examine how second language learners use language and how their language develops over time, and I explore how computational methods and AI-assisted technologies can support language learning, teaching, research, and assessment, as well as how AI can be used critically and in research-informed ways in language education.
